Ticket: #37 Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema

The pull request for this ticket has a RED build. Your job is to make it
green, on the branch you are already on, and nothing else.

The ticket's branch is checked out with write access at /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/731af3b41fc5/workspace/target.
Run every command from inside it (`cd /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/731af3b41fc5/workspace/target` first). The ticket
is at `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/731af3b41fc5/workspace/ticket.md`: read it before anything else. Pass `repo` (the
owner/name your task names above) on every `lore_*` call: the gateway has
no checkout to detect it from.

CI is the judge of this branch, and the `CI reported failures` section
of `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/731af3b41fc5/workspace/round-brief.md` is its verdict: the sha it judged, the checks that failed, and for
each — when CI published them — the annotations (`path:line message`),
the step that failed, and what it printed. Start from it, not from a
full local build.

WHEN THE VERDICT NAMES A FILE AND LINE — an annotation such as
`specs/x/spec.md:7 Status "draft" does not match ...` — open that file
at that line and fix what it says. Do not install dependencies, build
the workspace, or run the suite to confirm a finding CI already made
about a specific line; a lint or status error on a markdown file needs
an editor, not `npm ci`. Run a command only when the FIX needs one: a
test you must see fail, a typecheck of a package whose code you changed.
When that command's toolchain is not in this pod (`java`, `mvn`,
`gradle`, `go`, `cargo` or `dotnet` is not found), do not look for it and
do not install it: fix from the verdict, push, and let CI judge the push.

When it names the failed STEP and what that step printed but no
annotation, that is the diagnosis: find that step in
`.github/workflows/` and run only that step's command. When it names
only a check, map the check name to the job that publishes it, find the
command that job runs, and run ONLY that. Reproducing the whole build to
rediscover what you have already been told costs the ticket a pod and
tells you nothing new. The pod's Bash hook refuses a test runner given
no path, no workspace flag and no `cd` into the step's directory, so a
repo-wide `vitest run` never starts.

RUN A STEP'S COMMAND WHERE CI RAN IT, never from wherever your shell
happens to be. When the report says `Ran as: npm script <script> of
package <package>` (`npm_script` in `lore_get_ci_failures`), run
`npm run <script> -w <package>` from the repository root — or plain
`npm run <script>` if <package> is the root package.json's own name.
For any other step, take the directory from the workflow step itself
(its `working-directory:`, a `cd`, or a `-w`/`--prefix` in its `run:`).
A package's test command run at the repo root is NOT that command:
`npx vitest run` there discovers every package's suite. Run 754cb4fa ran
nine suites with coverage for 43 minutes and hit its deadline answering
what one package's suite answers in minutes.

NEVER RUN THE LINTER IN THIS POD, scoped or not. CI ran it on a machine
sized for it; here a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against a 1Gi
pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on it. When the red
check is a lint or format job, its findings are what you fix, not what
you reproduce: take the file and line from the annotation, or ask CI
with `lore_get_ci_failures` and then `lore_get_ci_job_log` with
`grep: "error"`. Format only the files this branch changed
(`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`); typecheck nothing here —
CI's build step already did, and it does not fit this pod.

IF THE SECTION IS MISSING OR TOO THIN, ASK CI YOURSELF: call
`lore_get_ci_failures` with `repo` (owner/name) and `branch` (the output
of `git branch --show-current`) — it reports on that branch: the judged
sha, the conclusion, and each failed check with its annotations, failed
steps and log tail. When a failure needs more of its log, call
`lore_get_ci_job_log` with `repo` and that failure's `job_id`, a `grep`
for the report's error marker (`error`, `FAIL`, `✖`) and a small `tail`.
Never reinstall or rebuild the workspace to learn what CI already
printed.

FIRST, check the branch has not moved since CI judged it. The section's
heading names the sha CI read (`judged_sha` from `lore_get_ci_failures`
when the section is absent); run `git log --format=%s <that sha>..HEAD`.
If any commit it lists does not carry `[skip ci]`,
the branch moved after CI judged it: somebody pushed, and CI has not
judged the new head yet.
Change nothing and run nothing, and end with
LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"ci_fixed":"branch moved past <sha>; CI re-judges the head"}}
The wait re-reads CI on the new head and sends the branch back here only
if that is red too.

BEFORE YOU READ ANY FILE, ask the graph what has failed here before.
For every path the red output names, call `lore-query-trace` with
`failures_touching` set to that path. Each row is a previous failed
attempt on that file: what failed, on which commit, and — when a later
attempt fixed it — the sha that did. `git show` that sha. This repo has
very likely hit this exact error before, and the diff that ended it last
time is the cheapest thing you will read today.

A row that says `still open` was never fixed; treat it as a warning that
the obvious fix did not work before, not as a solution to copy.

RULES:
- Fix EVERY finding the verdict names, in this visit, in the order
  listed. There is no local re-run here that would reveal the rest, and
  each finding you leave costs the ticket a round: run 2a291314's repair
  fixed one of three and the build came back red twice more. Do not add
  speculative fixes for failures the verdict did not name.
- Fix the cause, not the symptom. Never delete, skip, `.only`, `.todo` or
  loosen a test to go green; never widen a type to `any` to silence a
  typecheck error; never add an eslint-disable to pass lint. If the test
  is genuinely wrong, say why in your final message before you change it.
- Change only what the red build requires. Unrelated edits make the
  re-review harder and are not what was asked.
- If the named check's command passes locally, say exactly what you ran
  and what passed — the failure may be environment-only, and that is a
  finding, not a fix.

DELIVERY, NON-NEGOTIABLE — the next step runs in a DIFFERENT container:
- Before you commit, run the repository's FORMATTER over the files you
  changed (`npx prettier --write <files>`, `gofmt -w <files>`, whichever
  this repo uses) and nothing else from CI's checklist. Do NOT run the
  linter in this pod: CI runs it on every push, and here it does not
  fit — in this repository a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against
  a 1Gi pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on exactly
  that. A lint finding comes back as a red build naming the file and
  line, which the next round fixes with an editor.
- Do NOT typecheck here either. A green test is not a compiled build —
  vitest transpiles each file without checking types — but CI's build
  step is what proves it, and in this repository `tsc --noEmit` on
  `libs/shared` peaks near 950 MB against the 1Gi pod: run 2a291314's
  dod pod was OOM-killed on it. A type error comes back as a red build
  whose failed step and log tail name the file and line; the next
  round fixes it there. Read your imports and signatures twice instead.
- NEVER run a workspace build in this pod (`npm run build`, `tsc -b`, a
  `tsc` without `--noEmit`): tests resolve every workspace package from
  SOURCE, so nothing needs building for a test to see your change, and
  the build is the 950 MB step that OOM-killed run abac6ee9 while it
  rebuilt libs/shared for a test that never needed it.
- When the work is done, `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/731af3b41fc5/workspace/target add` what you changed and commit it with a
  short, factual message. Then `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/731af3b41fc5/workspace/target push origin HEAD`. The clone carries
  its own credentials, so a plain push authenticates; you need no token
  and must never look for one.
- Then bring the branch up to date with its base — `git fetch origin main`
  and merge `origin/main` in — and push again if that produced anything.
  A branch that cannot merge cleanly gets NO CI AT ALL: GitHub runs no
  workflow on a conflicted pull request, so the ticket parks on a build
  that will never start. Resolve any conflict now, favouring `origin/main`
  for anything this ticket did not write, and never by discarding your own
  work. This is why a nine-day-old branch stalled: 186 commits of drift,
  no checks, and a wait with nothing to wait for.
- Confirm it landed: `git status` must report the branch is not ahead of
  its upstream. An unpushed commit lives only in this container and
  dies with it — do NOT report success for one.
- If you changed nothing because the branch moved, end as the FIRST check
  above says. If you changed nothing for any other reason, say why and
  report `changes_requested` below, never `failed`: a failed repair ends
  the ticket, and the branch may already be green.
- Do not open a pull request: you have no `gh` and no GitHub token. Lore
  opens the PR from the branch you push.

Print exactly one of these as the last line of your final message:
- You reproduced a failure, fixed it, and the build passes locally:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"ci_fixed":"<one line: what was broken>"}}
- You could not make it green, or the failure is not in this repository:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"changes_requested","extras":{"ci_blocked":"<one line: what you ran and what stayed red>"}}

# Tool Input Validation

| Field  | Value                |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |
| Status | Shipped              |

Every tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor ([validated by: passes valid input including undeclared extra properties through to the executor without coercing or applying defaults](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L29)). When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).

## Validation at execute time

- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).
- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46), [validated by: rejects an invalid enum value naming the field and allowed values without leaking the offending value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L63)).
- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults ([validated by: passes valid input including undeclared extra properties through to the executor without coercing or applying defaults](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L29)).
- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake ([validated by: throws Unknown tool when execute is called with an unregistered tool name](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L110)).

## Schema compilation and caching

- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94), [validated by: throws at registration time naming the tool for an uncompilable schema](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L9)).
- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: compiles a static tool inputSchema once at register time and does not re-read it on execute](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L116)).
- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: validates against the current schema of a function-valued ToolDefinitionSource and caches validators by schema reference](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L162)).

## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery

- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).

- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: compiles a static tool inputSchema once at register time and does not re-read it on execute](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L119)).
- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: validates against the current schema of a function-valued ToolDefinitionSource and caches validators by schema reference](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L166)).

## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery

- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).

# Definition of Done

> `ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
> without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
> Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
> providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model.

**Strategy: `direct`** — `ToolRegistry.register`, `ToolRegistry.execute` and `createChatOrchestrator` already expose the exact entry points this ticket changes, so the acceptance tests call them directly today and fail because schema compilation and input validation are absent.

## Done when these pass

- [x] **rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor** — `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against `inputSchema`, returns a `ToolResponse` naming the missing required property, and does not invoke the executor.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs** — `ToolRegistry.execute` rejects a property with the wrong JSON Schema type without calling the executor, names the failing field path and expected type in `result`, and omits the offending property value from both `result` and emitted log lines.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled** — `ToolRegistry.register` compiles a static `ToolDefinition`'s `inputSchema` once at registration time and throws synchronously naming the tool when the schema is invalid.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round** — `createChatOrchestrator` feeds a schema-rejected tool call's `ToolResponse.result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` without invoking the executor on the invalid call, allowing the model to retry with valid arguments and complete the turn.
      `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [x] Add `ajv` to `dependencies` in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (`strict: false`, `validateFormats: false`, no coercion, no defaults, no injected `additionalProperties: false`) and bump the package version `MINOR`.
- [x] Compile `ToolDefinition.inputSchema` at `ToolRegistry.register` time (throwing an error naming the tool on invalid schemas) with unit test coverage in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts`.
- [x] Validate `input` in `ToolRegistry.execute` before invoking the executor (reusing the precompiled validator for static tools and caching compiled validators for function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` schemas by schema object reference in a `WeakMap`), returning a `ToolResponse` (`{result}`) that names failing field paths and expected types/required fields without echoing or logging offending values, and add the one-line doc comment pointing at `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`.
- [x] Add remaining unit tests in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` and `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts`, link the remaining statements in `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`, and update `example/weather-tool.ts`, `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md`, `.specify/spec.md`, `adrs/ADR-002-response-validation.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Out of scope

- Output validation and domain sanity checks (covered by ADR-002), MCP tool-server discovery and proxying (#42), per-tool authorization or `beforeToolCall` hooks (#40), retry/timeout/rate-limiting around tool execution, and concrete tool implementations.
